input.quote: (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder.
input.rationale: Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side indemnity in our favour (Services, Auction Platform, breach of representation or warranty, Kubient's and its subcontractors' acts or omissions), Section 11 supplies standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the damages limitation so the indemnity is uncapped. However, the enumerated prongs (p0048-p0051) contain no express intellectual-property infringement trigger, nor express breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data incident or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers. IP claims are reached only indirectly, via the broad "Services"/"Auction Platform" wording or by first proving breach of the Section 9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty (p0033) - a route that lets Kubient argue an IP claim is outside the indemnity or requires proof of warranty breach before defence is owed. The playbook requires the provider to stand behind third-party IP claims on the face of the indemnity, so we add an express prong (vi) for IP infringement plus (vii) breach of Law, (viii) Kubient-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, and (ix) gross negligence or wilful misconduct. This is a clarifying addition consistent with warranties Kubient has already given (p0033, p0035, p0037, p0041) and should be uncontroversial; if Kubient resists, our fallback is the IP prong alone with the usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. Spot-check on the reciprocal side: AP's Section 10(b) indemnity (p0052) runs wider than the preferred "Customer content / Customer breach of law" limit, extending to AP's unauthorised or inappropriate use of the Services and Auction Platform, breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of AP and its contractors; we have left it untouched because it mirrors Kubient's own prongs and reopening it would invite reciprocal narrowing of the Vendor indemnity we are strengthening.

proposal.summary: Add express IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct prongs to Kubient's Section 10(a) indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added express prongs to Kubient's indemnity so it clearly covers allegations that the Service, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe third-party IP rights, as well as Kubient's breach of Law, Kubient-caused data incidents and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Our playbook requires the provider to stand behind third-party IP claims on the face of the indemnity rather than only by implication through the Section 9(b)(i) warranty.

ops.text: (vi) any allegation that the Service, the Auction Platform or any deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other intellectual property or proprietary right of any third party; (vii) Kubient's breach of applicable Law; (viii) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer's data or Confidential Information caused by Kubient; or (ix) Kubient's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
